travelled to Westminster Station where the latter man left and the other two after speaking to a policeman visited for 5 minutes Westminster Hall, St. Margaret's Street, then lunched at Express Dairy Café, where HOBANN wrote a letter and posted same. They then proceeded to 21/24, Cockspur Street where they remained from 2.0. to 3.0. p.m., and afterwards visited the Royal Institute of International Affairs, Chatham House, 10, St. James' Square from 3.10. to 3.50. At 4.9. HODANN despatched a telegram from the Post Office 40/41, Fleet Street, E.C., afterwards both visited for 5 minutes the offices of the Manchester Guardian, 40/43, Fleet Street, Faith Bros. (Gents Outfitters) Furnival Street, then made an enquiry at First Avenue House, High Holborn, evidently wanting an address as HODANN carried a letter of which part of the address read "Alice -----The Bodley Head" (?this may relate to Lane (John) The Bodley Head Ltd., Publishers, Vigo Street). At 6.5. both entered 180, Regents Park Road and at 6.30. NILSSON left there with a man age 23, dressed plus fours, no hat, of foreign appearance, and both returned 25 minutes later. At 7.30. HODANN and NILSSON left and after making phone call dined at Criterion Brasserie, Jermyn Street, then to All, then to All Peoples Association, 9, Arlington Street, W. from 8.45. to 10.10 p.m. At the latter address a meeting was apparently being held, a large number of women and a few men were seen to enter and leave. HODANN and NILSSON returned home at 10.55.

Friday 29th March.

HODANN with child left home at 12.10 p.m. and after visiting Natural History Museum and Lyons Café, they returned to their address. At 1.35. HODANN again left, carrying despatch case, and went to Harlington Court, Lansdowne Road, South Lambeth where he remained from 2.5. to 3.35 p.m. when he left with NILSSON and both went to Chatham House,
